title: Finite affine restricted quotients and their schematic image neighbourhoods
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $T$ an affine $S$-scheme, $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $f:X\to T$ a morphism such that every representable etale scheme chart of $X$ is locally quasi-finite over $T$ [pqf-def-quasifinite] and $\Delta_{X/T}$ is a closed immersion on every scheme test [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose $p:h_U\to X$ is a representable surjective etale atlas [def-weil-etale-morphism], with $U$ affine, and its kernel pair $R=U\times_XU$ is affine with projections $s,t$ and a closed immersion $(s,t):R\to U\times_TU$. Suppose the fppf sheaf quotient $U/R$ is identified with $X$ over $T$, compatibly with $p$; the quotient is the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] on [def-pc-fppf-site] of $H\mapsto U(H)/R(H)$. For every $u\in U$, let $x=p(u)$ and $q=f(x)$. There exist an affine scheme $T'$, an etale morphism $T'\to T$, a point $q'\in T'$ over $q$ with $\kappa(q')\cong\kappa(q)$ [def-weil-residue-field], a point $u'$ over $u$ and $q'$, and open and closed decompositions $U\times_TT'=U'\amalg A$, $R\times_TT'=R'\amalg B$, such that $u'\in U'$, $U',R'$ are finite over $T'$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and $R'$ is the full restricted relation on $U'$. The schemes $U',R'$ are affine and the restricted projections are finite locally free and etale [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. The fppf quotient $Q=U'/R'$ is an affine $T'$-scheme whose canonical map into $X\times_TT'$ identifies $h_Q$ with an open subspace $V'$. There is an open subspace $W\subseteq X$ represented by a scheme, with $|W|$ equal to the image of $|V'|\to|X|$ and $x\in|W|$ [def-a1-space-open-subspace]. Here open and closed subschemes have their induced structures [def-weil-open-immersion], and $|X|$ and $|V'|$ mean field-valued point classes [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes].

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-etale-atlas-presentation] to $p$. It identifies $R(H)$ with pairs having the same image in $X(H)$ and gives surjective etale projections $s,t$. These pairs also have the same $T$-image, so on $T$-schemes this is an equivalence relation in $U\times_TU$. The chartwise hypothesis applied to $p$ gives that $U\to T$ is locally quasi-finite. Thus all hypotheses of [lem-a1-proper-etale-relation-finite-neighbourhood] hold: $T,U,R$ are affine, $s,t$ are etale over $T$, and the relation map is the assumed closed immersion. That node supplies $T',q',u',U',R'$ and both clopen decompositions, the residue-field isomorphism, finiteness over $T'$, and the full restricted equivalence relation with etale projections.

source.place: Tag 03XX (proposition-locally-quasi-finite-separated-over-scheme), fourth and final proof paragraphs

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](b), $U'$ and $R'$ are affine because they are finite over the affine $T'$. Each restricted projection is a $T'$-morphism between schemes finite over $T'$, so the last clause of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-permanence-over-separated] makes it finite. Each is etale by step 1, hence flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Together with finiteness, this is exactly finite local freeness in [def-pc-finite-locally-free].

source.place: Tag 03XX (proposition-locally-quasi-finite-separated-over-scheme), fourth and final proof paragraphs

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-finite-flat-affine-relation-quotient] over S after transporting the affine schemes U′ and R′ to their canonical spectra. Transport its quotient map and coequalizer universal property back along the affine isomorphisms. The U′-to-T′ structure map coequalizes the restricted projections. Since the representable of T′ is an fppf sheaf, the quotient universal property descends it uniquely to Q-to-T′; Yoneda turns this natural transformation into a scheme morphism.

source.place: Tag 03XX (proposition-locally-quasi-finite-separated-over-scheme), fourth and final proof paragraphs

proof.text: Compute the base-changed atlas and its kernel pair by the pullback universal property, directly in presheaves. Use universal_locally_surjective from [lem-trf-etale-relation-finding-opens] for the given universal property of the original quotient to obtain local surjectivity: the subsheaf locally generated by its image admits a retraction, hence equals X. Local surjectivity survives pullback. A map out of the base-changed atlas equalizing its kernel pair descends uniquely by sheaf gluing on its covering image sieves; thus the base-changed sheaf has the required quotient universal property. The full-restriction clause of step 1 gives a kernel pair for U′-to-X_T′. Compare this with the canonical iterated-pullback restriction, transport the affine quotient universal property across their unique isomorphism, and apply [lem-trf-etale-relation-finding-opens]. The full projections are surjective etale by the scheme-test property of the base-changed atlas, and the clopen inclusion is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. This yields the canonical open immersion Q-to-X_T′.

source.place: Tag 03XX (proposition-locally-quasi-finite-separated-over-scheme), fourth and final proof paragraphs

proof.text: The structure morphism $Q\to T'$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], since both schemes are affine. It is consequently quasi-affine in the precise sense required by [lem-a1-etale-quasi-affine-image-scheme]: factor it as the identity open immersion $Q\to Q$ followed by this affine morphism. The identity is quasi-compact since its inverse image on every quasi-compact open is that same open. Apply that node to the given separated chartwise locally quasi-finite $X\to T$, the affine etale $T'\to T$ of step 1, and $V'\cong h_Q$. It gives an open subspace $W\subseteq X$ represented by a scheme, whose point set is exactly the image of $|V'|\to|X|$.

source.place: Tag 03XX (proposition-locally-quasi-finite-separated-over-scheme), fourth and final proof paragraphs

proof.text: The residue-field point $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u')\to U'$ followed by its quotient map defines a field-valued point of $V'$. Its image in $X$ is the image of the point $u$ because $u'$ lies over $u$ and all quotient maps above are induced by the atlas. In field-valued point classes [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes], extension from $\kappa(u)$ to $\kappa(u')$ leaves this class unchanged. Thus this image is $x=p(u)$, and the equality of point sets in step 5 implies $x\in|W|$. This proves the last clause and finishes the assembly.
